items.title: rustel
items.author: Curator
items.content:
rustel is a terminal studio and TUI for live-coding music with the Strudel pattern language.

The studio features a live strudel code editor, a mixer, synths and sample playback, with Csound orchestras and support for VST3 instruments and effects. It shows the notes being played and graphs of the sound and you can edit the code while the music plays. It also includes a sample browser for previewing sounds if you're curious about the sample library.

This tool also supports MIDI and OSC output, Ableton Link synchronization with other music software, themes, WAV or MP3 export and edit recovery. If an edit fails, rustel keeps playing the previous version. Its session tapes record applied code changes and their timing for replay. File watching reloads code saved from external editors during playback.

rustel is ideal for programmers, musicians and hobbyists interested in live coding and algorithmic music. It is practical for composing tracks, experimenting with sound and performing sets in a terminal environment.

items.title: adbtop
items.author: Curator
items.content:
adbtop is both CLI and TUI for monitoring Android app performance through Android Debug Bridge (adb) in the terminal.

It can chart CPU and memory use for one app running on the device or the whole phone, alongside device statistics such as battery level and temperature. The CPU view shows activity for each core and thread and for individual apps, it reports frame rates and frames that take too long to draw.

Users can launch or stop apps, measure startup times and test power-saving settings. The CLI saves JSON reports and CSV samples, including measurements taken after actions such as opening a screen. It also can be used to purposefully set limits on  automated checks at runtime when properties such as memory, hangs or response time exceed certain limits set by the user.

For Android developers, testers and QA engineers, adbtop is useful for investigating resource usage during app interactions, checking for memory leaks and testing performance issues before a release.

items.title: rumdl
items.author: Curator
items.content:
rumdl is a high performance command-line tool for linting and formatting Markdown files.

It checks for the headings, lists, links and code blocks content of a markdown file and reports rule names in the MDXXX format. A diff mode previews fixes before files change or applied and formatting, applies available fixes and may succeed with unresolved issues. Check mode returns a exit code for remaining violations in the document.

This tool discovers common markdownlint configuration files and adjusts rules for Markdown flavors such as MkDocs and MDX. Its language server applies configured checks inside editors, and pre-commit hooks or CI integrations run them against repository changes.

For developers, technical writers and documentation maintainers, rumdl helps keep Markdown files cleanly formatted and consistent across a project. It it is also useful for pre-commit checks after editing, before committing changes and catching formatting errors in the CI.

items.title: tidemail
items.author: Curator
items.content:
tidemail is a CLI and TUI for reading, writing and managing email from several accounts.

It supports Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Outlook and custom IMAP/SMTP providers and its interface shows accounts, folders, message lists and can open emails on one screen. Users can view all accounts in one inbox, search downloaded mail, add labels, archive and move or delete several messages together with bulk actions. It can preview pictures inside of emails in a supported terminal with Kitty graphics such as Ghostty, Rio or WezTerm, and only loads pictures from websites with permission from the user.

Other features include support for file attachments, automatic draft saving, saved replies, optional spell checking and custom themes. It waits five seconds by default before sending an email, so users have a change to cancel it. It also reads downloaded mail, prepares drafts and sends messages with JSON results for optional scripting use-cases.

For those who prefer handling email in the terminal, tidemail is ideal if you are looking for a unified inbox for multiple accounts without needing to use configuration files.

items.title: rat-commander
items.author: Curator
items.content:
rat-commander is an all-in-one two-panel terminal file manager for browsing and manipulating local and remote files.

Its interface is heavily inspired by midnight-commander with a two-pane window setting which you can copy, move or delete files between panels, and transfers files across storage devices in a progress window with a graphical speed chart. It can connect to remote hosts and mount directories via SFTP, SCP, FTP locations into the same panels and transfers normal file operations.

What differentiates rat-commander is its command palette with over 100+ available operations, alongside several built-in tools such as a disk explorer showing the largest files indexed on disk, network connections inspector for active connections and a process explorer showing the list of all running processes on the machine. This tool has multiple preview views including a detail, tree, 3D view and a thumbnail view when showing the selected file or directory.

Ideal for system administrators, software engineers and developers used to mc, rat-commander provides a similar two-panel file management across local folders and remote servers, whilst providing more built-in useful utilities included.

items.title: dasel
items.author: Curator
items.content:
dasel is a command-line tool for querying, modifying and converting structured data.

It uses the same selector syntax across JSON, YAML, TOML, CSV and other formats. Queries traverse nested objects or search for values matching a condition, and separate input and output formats enable composability uses in shell pipelines, CI/CD builds and in scripting use-cases for automation. 

dasel goes further than jq by having a built-in environment that allows for testing multiple dataset formats with a rapid feedback and response loop in the live preview in the query. Assignments in dasel change selected values, including values derived from each item in a collection.

This tool is very useful towards developers, data engineers and system administrators who already use jq for JSON but need an alternative that supports multiple formats including JSON but also handle YAML or TOML, CSV and more for scripting and automation.
